subject: Vocabulary
description: Latin SCRIB/SCRIPT roots (write) — manuscript, transcribe, prescription, conscription, postscript, describe, ascribe.

questions.stem: SCRIBE/SCRIPT root means 'write'. MANUSCRIPT literally means:
questions.explanation: MANUSCRIPT — etymology MANU (hand, Latin) + SCRIPTUS (written, from scribere) = 'WRITTEN BY HAND'. Originally meant any HANDWRITTEN document; modern usage extends to ANY DRAFT/UNPUBLISHED document submitted to a publisher (even typed/computerized). WORD FAMILY (root SCRIBE/SCRIPT = write): (1) MANUSCRIPT — handwritten document. (2) DESCRIBE — write down/express. (3) PRESCRIBE — write before (e.g., doctor's prescription). (4) PRESCRIPTION — what's prescribed (medical, legal). (5) PROSCRIBE — write against (forbid by law). (6) PROSCRIPTION — banishment. (7) ASCRIBE — assign/attribute. (8) SUBSCRIBE — sign under (newspaper subscription). (9) TRANSCRIBE — write across (= copy/transfer text). (10) CONSCRIPT — write together (forced enrollment, military draft). (11) INSCRIBE — write into. (12) CIRCUMSCRIBE — write around (limit). (13) POSTSCRIPT (P.S.) — written after. (14) NONDESCRIPT — not describable; unremarkable. (15) SCRIPT — written text (esp. for film/play). (16) SCRIBBLE — write hurriedly/messily. (17) SCRIPTURE — sacred writing. (18) SCRIBE — professional writer/copyist. (19) SCRIPTORIUM — room for writing (medieval monasteries). (20) MANUSCRIPT culture: pre-printing era, monasteries hand-copied books. INDIA's MANUSCRIPT HERITAGE: ~5 MILLION manuscripts on palm-leaf, birch-bark, paper; mostly Sanskrit, Persian, Pali, Tamil, Telugu, etc. NATIONAL MISSION FOR MANUSCRIPTS (NAMAMI, 2003) — preserves these. UPSC angle: manuscript preservation in cultural heritage. PYQ FREQUENCY: SCRIBE root vocab in SSC CGL, CAT, UPSC English 1-2× per cycle.

questions.explanation: TRANSCRIBE — etymology TRANS (across, Latin) + SCRIBE (write) = 'write across' = CONVERT one form to another (typically: speech → written; or one written form to another). USES: (1) TRANSCRIPTION of audio interviews → written text (journalism, academia, courts). (2) MEDICAL TRANSCRIPTION — doctor's notes/dictation → patient records. (3) MUSICAL TRANSCRIPTION — converting music to written notation; or piece for one instrument adapted for another. (4) BIOLOGICAL TRANSCRIPTION — DNA → mRNA in genetics (a different but analogous use). (5) PHONETIC TRANSCRIPTION — speech sound → IPA symbols (linguistics). DON'T CONFUSE: (a) TRANSCRIBE — change form (speech → text, etc.). (b) TRANSLATE — change LANGUAGE (e.g., English → Hindi). (c) TRANSLITERATE — change SCRIPT (e.g., Devanagari → Roman). EXAM TRAP: TRANSCRIBE vs TRANSLATE vs TRANSLITERATE — three distinct operations! INDIA AI: TRANSCRIPTION services use AI/ML — Otter.ai, Google Speech-to-Text; major productivity tool. JOBS: medical-transcription industry employs ~50,000 in India. UPSC angle: language preservation — esp. ENDANGERED LANGUAGES; UNESCO Atlas of World Languages in Danger lists ~200 Indian languages as endangered. PYQ FREQUENCY: transcribe vs translate distinction in SSC CGL Tier 2, IBPS PO, CAT 1× per cycle.

questions.explanation: PRESCRIBE — etymology PRE (before) + SCRIBE (write) = 'WRITE BEFORE' or 'AUTHORITATIVELY ORDER'. KEY USES: (1) MEDICAL: doctor PRESCRIBES medication = formally orders it for a patient. NOUN: PRESCRIPTION = the written order (Rx). India: only registered MD/MBBS doctors can prescribe (under MCI/NMC rules). (2) LEGAL: rule/regulation 'as prescribed' = as defined by law/authority. (3) GENERAL: 'doctor prescribes rest' = recommends. CONTRAST WITH PROSCRIBE (different word!): PRESCRIBE = ORDER (positive); PROSCRIBE = FORBID (negative, ban). 'The govt PROSCRIBED the organization' = banned. PROSCRIPTION (noun) = ban. KEY DISTINCTION (UPSC trap): (1) PRE-scribe — write BEFORE/AHEAD = recommend, order. (2) PRO-scribe — write AGAINST = forbid. RX SYMBOL: 'Rx' on prescription comes from Latin 'recipe' = 'take' (imperative — take this medication). ABUSE of medical PRESCRIPTION authority: 'over-prescription' of antibiotics → ANTIMICROBIAL RESISTANCE — major UPSC GS-3 health concern. INDIA's NATIONAL ACTION PLAN ON ANTIMICROBIAL RESISTANCE (NAP-AMR, 2017). KEY DRUG REGULATION INDIA: Drugs Controller General (DCGI), Ministry of Health, ICMR — oversee prescription rules. UPSC angle: health policy + drug regulation in GS-2/3. PYQ FREQUENCY: PRESCRIBE vs PROSCRIBE distinction in SSC CGL, CAT, UPSC English 1× per cycle.

questions.explanation: CONSCRIPTION — etymology CON (together) + SCRIPT (write) = 'WRITE/ENROLL TOGETHER' = forced/mandatory enrollment in military service. Also called 'THE DRAFT'. CONTRAST: VOLUNTARY enlistment. COUNTRIES with conscription (current/historical): (1) ISRAEL — Israeli Defense Forces; men + women required to serve (2-3 years). (2) SOUTH KOREA — ~2-year military service for men. (3) NORTH KOREA — 7-10 years!. (4) SWITZERLAND, FINLAND, NORWAY, AUSTRIA, RUSSIA, IRAN — currently maintain. (5) USA — ended 1973 (Vietnam-era end); now all-volunteer. Selective Service registration still required for males 18-25. (6) UK — ended 1960. (7) FRANCE — ended 1996; reintroduced limited service 2019. INDIA: NEVER had conscription. India has all-VOLUNTEER military force (largest volunteer army in world ~1.4 million active personnel). RECENT — 'AGNIPATH SCHEME' (2022) — short-term (4-year) military recruitment scheme. NOT conscription, but reduced-tenure ENLISTMENT. Controversial; ongoing reviews. RELATED CONCEPTS: (a) DESERTION — leaving military without permission. (b) PACIFISM — opposition to all violence/war. (c) CONSCIENTIOUS OBJECTOR — refuses military service on moral/religious grounds. WORLD WARS: massive conscription waves; e.g., USA Civil War 1863, WWI/II — millions drafted. UPSC angle: defence reforms + 'jobs in armed forces' issue. PYQ FREQUENCY: conscription concept in CAT, advanced UPSC English 1× per 2 cycles.

questions.stem: POSTSCRIPT (P.S.) at end of letter literally means:
questions.explanation: POSTSCRIPT (P.S.) — etymology POST (after, Latin) + SCRIPT (written) = 'WRITTEN AFTER'. ABBREVIATED 'P.S.' Used in LETTERS to add information AFTER the main body + signature. EXAMPLE: 'Dear Mom, ... your loving son, Ravi. P.S. Please send the cake recipe.' KEY USES: (1) AFTERTHOUGHTS — info forgotten in main letter. (2) EMPHASIS — highlight a single key point. (3) Personal/informal touch. P.P.S. (POST-POSTSCRIPT) — added AFTER P.S. (Latin: 'post post scriptum'). ETYMOLOGY of 'POST' prefix: (1) POST = AFTER (postpone, postdate, posthumous). (2) Note: 'post' as 'mail/place' is from Italian 'posta' → station. POST WORD FAMILY: (a) POSTPONE — put after (delay). (b) POSTHUMOUS — after death. (c) POSTERITY — those born after (descendants). (d) POST-MORTEM — after death (medical autopsy). (e) POSTGRADUATE — after graduation. (f) POSTERIOR — back/rear. KEY MODERN USAGE: digital communications (emails) replaced traditional P.S. concept. But still common in informal letters, gift-cards, formal correspondence. PRACTICE — VOCABULARY-style: (a) 'POSTHUMOUS award' = award given after one's death. (b) 'POST-MORTEM' = examination of body to determine cause of death. (c) 'POSTERITY will judge' = future generations. (d) 'POSTNUPTIAL agreement' = signed after marriage. UPSC angle: legal/medical vocabulary; CSAT comprehension. PYQ FREQUENCY: post- prefix vocab in CAT, UPSC English 1× per cycle.

questions.explanation: INSCRIPTION — etymology IN (into) + SCRIPT (write) = 'WRITTEN INTO/ENGRAVED'. Refers to text engraved/carved on STONE, METAL, MONUMENT, or other hard surface; long-lasting, formal. EPIGRAPHY = study of ancient inscriptions. INDIA's RICH INSCRIPTION TRADITION: (1) ASHOKAN ROCK + PILLAR EDICTS (3rd c. BCE) — earliest deciphered Indian inscriptions; in BRAHMI (most), KHAROSHTHI (NW), GREEK + ARAMAIC (Kandahar). 14 major rock edicts + minor edicts; on EDICTS Ashoka spread DHAMMA (Buddhism). KEY INSCRIPTIONS: (a) GIRNAR (Gujarat) — Ashoka. (b) DELHI-TOPRA, DELHI-MEERUT — pillar edicts. (c) RUMMINDEI (Lumbini, Nepal) — Buddha's birthplace. (2) HATHIGUMPHA INSCRIPTION (Odisha, ~1st c. BCE) — KHARAVELA of Kalinga. (3) JUNAGADH INSCRIPTION of RUDRADAMAN I (~150 CE, Sanskrit). (4) ALLAHABAD PRASHASTI / PILLAR INSCRIPTION (~340 CE, by HARISENA on Samudragupta) — Sanskrit; Sanskrit-Brahmi. (5) AIHOLE PRASHASTI (~634 CE, by RAVIKIRTI on Pulakeshin II of Chalukyas) — earliest Sanskrit poem. (6) NAVARATNA INSCRIPTIONS — at Vikramaditya's court. ASHOKA SCRIPT DECIPHERMENT: by JAMES PRINSEP (1837, British scholar) — major breakthrough. UPSC angle: ANCIENT HISTORY GS-1; epigraphy + archaeology. CAREERS: ASI (Archaeological Survey of India) employs epigraphists. PYQ FREQUENCY: inscriptions in UPSC, MPSC, SSC ancient history 1-2× per cycle.

questions.explanation: ASCRIBE — etymology AD (to, towards) + SCRIBE (write) = 'WRITE TO' = ASSIGN, ATTRIBUTE. SAMPLE: 'She ascribed her success to hard work and luck.' 'The painting was ascribed to da Vinci' (attributed). NOUN: ASCRIPTION. SYNONYMS: attribute, credit, assign, impute, accredit. ANTONYMS: deny, dissociate. CONTRAST: (1) ASCRIBE — generally NEUTRAL or POSITIVE attribution. 'Success ascribed to teamwork.' (2) IMPUTE — often NEGATIVE attribution. 'Imputed bad motives to him.' (3) ATTRIBUTE — neutral, common alternative. (4) CREDIT — positive (credited HIM with the discovery). KEY 'AD-' words (root AD = to, towards, near): (a) ADHERE — stick to. (b) ADJUST — fit to. (c) ADJOIN — join to. (d) ADMINISTER — serve to. (e) ADVOCATE — speak for. (f) ADAPT — fit to. (g) ADJOURN — defer until later. (h) ADJACENT — lying next to. SOCIO-PSYCHOLOGICAL: 'ASCRIPTIVE STATUS' = social status assigned at BIRTH (caste, race, gender) — vs ACHIEVED status (education, occupation). UPSC angle: social stratification + sociology terms in GS-1; CASTE-based ascriptive social structure was a Constitutional concern (Articles 14-17 abolish untouchability). RELATED ATTRIBUTES vocab: (a) ATTRIBUTABLE — capable of being attributed. (b) ATTRIBUTABLE TO — caused by. (c) BY ATTRIBUTION — by assignment. PYQ FREQUENCY: ASCRIBE/IMPUTE/ATTRIBUTE distinctions in CAT, advanced UPSC English 1× per cycle.
